rule: Component != Pattern != Template. Components remain reusable surfaces; patterns own reusable process orchestration, policy, state, recovery, routing, data loading, and multi-component behavior; templates compose screens, IA, domain modules, and end-to-end product journeys from patterns.

component: A bounded reusable unit with local props, local states, and package-owned behavior.
It must not own process policy, data fetching, routing, or multi-step recovery.
If behavior needs cross-component orchestration, keep the component bounded and move orchestration to a pattern.
pattern: A reusable behavior contract that coordinates multiple components, policy, state transitions, recovery, accessibility, and responsive behavior.
It may be domain-specific when the behavior is reusable across templates or product areas, such as authentication, onboarding, bulk actions, administration, or permissions.
It is still a pattern when it governs a system rather than a final product screen, even if one template is the first consumer.
It must expose slots, dependencies, states, motion, MIEL, tests, and rejection rules.
template: A final product composition: one or more screens, IA, navigation, modules, domain data, and end-to-end task coverage.
It consumes patterns and components but does not redefine their contracts.
Domain dashboard pages or product modules belong to templates unless they introduce reusable interaction behavior beyond the screen composition.
classificationTests: If removing brand/domain data leaves a reusable interaction contract, classify as pattern.
If the artifact mostly arranges multiple patterns into a product screen or suite, classify as template.
If it can be shipped as one package factory with local props and no orchestration policy, classify as component.
If it is a domain system with state machine, policy, recovery, and reusable slots, classify as pattern even when it appears inside a template.

dialog.componentBoundary: Modal surface semantics, label, description, actions, open and closed state.
dialog.patternWork: Confirmation policy, irreversible action handling, financial or permission risk copy, and recovery system.
dialog.nextAction: Audit Confirmation Dialog docs against Dialog factory and add risk tiers, recovery, disabled action, and audit-copy requirements.

menu.componentBoundary: Compact contextual action list anchored to one trigger.
menu.patternWork: Command routing, permissions, shortcuts, destructive action hierarchy, and high-risk action alternatives.
menu.nextAction: Define where menu behavior is command palette, toolbar overflow, or mobile action sheet instead of adding routing to Menu.

drawer.componentBoundary: Side drawer surface with trigger, header, body, footer, and dialog semantics.
drawer.patternWork: Edit lifecycle, validation, submit, dirty state, close recovery, support handoff, and responsive drawer adaptation.
drawer.nextAction: Audit Drawer Adapter and admin flows for edit lifecycle and close recovery.

table.componentBoundary: Semantic table structure, columns, rows, local sort indicators, and selected row state.
table.patternWork: Remote data, virtualization, filtering, pagination, expansion, export, bulk actions, keyboard navigation, and row processs.
table.nextAction: Use Virtual Data Table as the primary replacement for Data Table behavior before dashboard tables are expanded.

bottom-sheet.componentBoundary: No public component boundary. Bottom Sheet is classified as a mobile pattern; any package factory is implementation support only.
bottom-sheet.patternWork: Mobile context preservation, action hierarchy, dismissal, focus restoration, drag/gesture behavior, safe-area layout, and desktop escalation.
bottom-sheet.nextAction: Move public docs to the Bottom Sheet pattern and keep Action Sheet / Fullscreen Sheet as more specific patterns built on the same mobile-sheet behavior.

biometric-prompt.componentBoundary: Local biometric prompt with icon, copy, primary action, fallback text, and explicit state.
biometric-prompt.patternWork: Authentication recovery, fallback routing, OTP handoff, passcode reset, lockout, risk escalation, and support recovery.
biometric-prompt.nextAction: Audit auth pattern to prove biometric prompt, Code input, error panel, and recovery states compose correctly.

tree-view.componentBoundary: Bounded tree semantics for one local hierarchy surface. Sidebar may inform visual hierarchy, but app navigation chrome remains the Sidebar pattern.
tree-view.patternWork: Permission editors, drag and drop, dependencies, multi-pane hierarchy processs, templates, review paths, and nested table rows.
tree-view.nextAction: Keep Tree View visually aligned with Sidebar hierarchy cues while routing permission editors, drag/drop, and TableTree/Data Table behavior to patterns.

motion-boundary.componentBoundary: One bounded region with explicit local motion state and reduced-motion signal.
motion-boundary.patternWork: Page choreography, route transitions, animation storytelling, sequencing, and cross-surface state.
motion-boundary.nextAction: Decide whether broader motion orchestration belongs to a foundation reference or a dedicated pattern before adding new docs.

animated-moment.componentBoundary: One bounded animation moment with label, state, and reduced-motion fallback.
animated-moment.patternWork: Onboarding, education, campaign, multi-step animation sequences, celebration timing, and completion storytelling.
animated-moment.nextAction: Decide whether animation storytelling should be documented as a pattern or governed by Illustration/Motion foundations.

nextBatch.reason: P0 risk from Dialog and Quick Action. High-risk actions need confirmation, copy, recovery, and tests before admin/mobile patterns expand.
P0 risk from Biometric Prompt, Code Input, Phone Input, Error Panel, and Animated Moment.
P0 risk from Table and dashboard/admin patterns. Prevents Data Table behavior from leaking back into component layer.
